name: When the Ground Moved: The Great Earthquakes
description: From Shaanxi in 1556 and Lisbon in 1755 to Tohoku in 2011: the earthquakes and tsunamis that broke cities, changed thinking and revealed how the Earth works.

checkpoints.name: Quakes of the old world
checkpoints.note: The 1556 Shaanxi earthquake in China is among the deadliest known. The 1755 Lisbon earthquake and tsunami shook Europe, and Voltaire used it to question easy optimism in the Enlightenment.

checkpoints.name: Quakes in modern cities
checkpoints.note: San Francisco in 1906 and the Great Kanto earthquake of 1923 around Tokyo and Yokohama broke modern cities and set off fires. Wegener proposed drifting continents.

checkpoints.name: The plates explain
checkpoints.note: The Valdivia earthquake in Chile in 1960 was the strongest ever recorded, and Alaska followed in 1964. These helped confirm plate tectonics, and the 1976 Tangshan earthquake in China was among the deadliest of the century.

checkpoints.name: Great waves
checkpoints.note: The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, the Sichuan quake in 2008, Haiti in 2010 and Tohoku in 2011 were huge disasters. Tohoku's tsunami also caused the Fukushima nuclear accident.
